targetAudience: Muslims who want a short, trustworthy daily reminder they can act on
topic: Why intentions matter in ordinary actions
coreInsight: The first hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari ties every deed to its intention, so an ordinary action can be done for Allah.
selectionRationale: Most relevant and clearest at a glance; the teaching pays it off.

script.onScreen: Same action. Different intention. / Pause for one second.
Intend it before you do it. / Share it with a friend

caption:
The same action can begin with a different intention.

The very first hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari is about intention.

Before your next task today, pause and set it for Allah.

Share it with a friend.

📖 Sources
• Sahih al-Bukhari 1 (Sahih, tr. Muhsin Khan) — sunnah.com/bukhari:1
Full text: Narrated 'Umar bin Al-Khattab: I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying, "The reward of deeds depends upon the intentions and every person will get the reward according to what he has intended. So whoever emigrated for worldly benefits or for a woman to marry, his emigration was for what he emigrated for
• Recitation: Qur'an 6:162 — Mahmoud Khalil Al-Husary (EveryAyah.com) — quran.com/6/162
